description: Navigation rails let people switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.

tags.devx:
- Treats `NavigationRailItem`, `NavigationRailSection`, and `Fab` specially.
- Selection is index-based; provide `selectedItem` for controlled usage.
- `footer` pins arbitrary content (e.g. a sign-out button) below the items,
  without needing to wrap the rail in a custom layout.
tags.a11y:
- The menu toggle button exposes its open/closed label via `menu.opened`/
  `menu.closed`; there is no additional live region for the extended state.
tags.limitations: - Keyboard navigation/roving tabindex is not implemented.

className.name: className
className.description: Root classes (string), static element classes (object), or state-aware element classes (function).

variant.name: variant
variant.description: Visual density of the rail; `modal` is meant for a temporary overlay presentation.

selectedItem.name: selectedItem
selectedItem.description: Controlled index of the selected item.

extended.name: extended
extended.description: Controlled extended state of the rail.

alignment.name: alignment
alignment.description: Vertical distribution of items: `top`-anchored or `middle` of the rail.

menu.name: menu
menu.description: Icon and label shown by the menu toggle button in each extended/closed state.

footer.name: footer
footer.description: Content pinned below the item list (e.g. an account or sign-out action).

tags.devx:
- Project `udx-navigation-rail-item`, `udx-navigation-rail-section`, and
  a `udx-fab` as children; the FAB is hoisted into the header.
- `footer` content is projected via `<div footer>`/an element with a
  `footer` attribute, pinned below the item list.
- Selection is index-based; use `selectedItem`/`selectedItemChange` for
  controlled usage, or `defaultSelectedItem` uncontrolled.
tags.a11y:
- The menu toggle button exposes its open/closed label via `menu.opened`/
  `menu.closed`.
tags.limitations:
- Keyboard navigation/roving tabindex is not implemented.
- Angular's `selectedItem`/`selectedItemChange` follow this repository's
  output-naming convention; React instead exposes a raw
  `setSelectedItem` dispatcher (an intentional platform difference, not a
  parity gap).
- `[class.x]` and `[ngClass]` bind to the `display: contents` host and have no visible effect; use `class`, `[class]`, or `classes`.
